name: TextArea
purpose: Let a user write or edit multi-line free text - notes, descriptions, comments - in a bordered, resizable field.
intent: The multi-line counterpart of Text Field: a real native <textarea> in the same bordered frame, sharing Text Field's size, appearance, invalid, and state treatment so the two read as one family. Grouped with Text Field as a molecule for that reason, though it composes no other component.

figmaSource.note: Filed on the file's own "🚧 Text Area" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin. The `sm` size was removed on 2026-08-27 (it read almost identically to md); the size axis is now md/lg. variantCount reflects that removal (was 96) and should be re-confirmed live next time the Components file is connected.
figmaSource.structure: One component set across six axes - `type` (default / rich-inline), `size` (md / lg), `tone` (default / subtle), `state` (default / hover / focus / typing / filled / autofill), `isDisabled`, `isInvalid`. Each variant is a single `Container` frame holding the text; the visual frame (fill, border, radius) is bound on the component node, not the inner Container (which carries only padding). Geometry measured per size: padding block/inline md 8/8, lg 12/12; radius lg (8) at md, xl (12) at lg; font body-md (14/24) at md, body-lg (16/24) at lg. State frame tokens (tone=default): default fill background/input/default + border/input 1px; hover fill background/input/hovered; focus fill background/input/pressed + border/focused 2px; typing border/focused 2px; filled + autofill = default; invalid border/error 2px; disabled background/disabled + border/disabled. tone=subtle has a transparent box with a bottom-only accent that reveals on hover (border/input) / focus (border/focused) / invalid (border/error), bottom corners square.
apiAdaptationNotes: Refactored from a bare <textarea> to a wrapper <div> pattern (matching Text Field) to support a trailing icon/action slot (iconAfter). The wrapper div gets the frame styling (border, background, radius, padding) and uses display: flex; align-items: flex-start to lay out the textarea and the optional action slot side by side. The textarea is a transparent, borderless child inside the wrapper, with flex: 1 1 auto. Focus detection uses :focus-within on the wrapper instead of :focus on the textarea. The browser's native resize grip still works: resize: inherit on the textarea, with overflow: auto on the wrapper's resize_* classes (CSS requires overflow != visible for resize to work on a div).

Added an iconAfter slot (React.ReactNode) for a trailing icon or interactive control (e.g. an edit pencil IconButton). Rendered in a span.action wrapper, flex: 0 0 auto. Not aria-hidden - it may hold a real focusable action. The inline appearance combined with iconAfter is the standard pattern for embedding inside a Key Value Pair.

Added a third appearance value, 'inline', for chromeless-at-rest embedding inside Key Value Pair wrapped in Inline Edit. Figma's 'context' axis (default/inline) maps here. Mirrors subtle's bottom-only border treatment but starts fully transparent at rest (no border or background). Hover shows the raised-surface hover background + a bottom accent (border/input), focus shows a bottom-only 2px focus border (border-bottom-color + bottom-only box-shadow, same technique as subtle), invalid shows a bottom-only error border, and disabled stays transparent. Top corners keep the size's radius; bottom corners are square — same shape as subtle. The field keeps its normal padding and height so it reads as a real input when activated.
Figma's `tone` axis is exposed in code as `appearance` (default/subtle/inline) - the same axis and the same name its sibling Text Field uses, so the two components share one vocabulary.

Figma binds a newer `background/input/*` + `border/focused` token naming that has no counterpart in this build. Those map one-to-one onto the `elevation/surface/raised/*` + `border/focus` semantic tokens Text Field already consumes (same intent), so Text Area reuses those rather than inventing unbacked tokens - keeping it visually identical to Text Field per token governance's reuse-first rule.

Focus and invalid replace the border color and paint the extra pixel via an inset box-shadow rather than a real 1px->2px border-width change - the same technique Text Field uses, so the multi-line text never shifts by a pixel on focus/blur or invalid toggle.

Figma tints the fill on focus (`background/input/pressed`); code deliberately keeps the resting fill on focus instead, matching Text Field's established no-tint-on-focus behavior (and that token does not exist here).

The `state` axis (hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill) is not a prop - those are live pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:focus`), with a documentation-only `data-force-state` pin mirroring them for static Storybook reference, exactly as Text Field, Button, and Checkbox do. `filled`, `typing`, and `autofill` need no distinct styling (they render as default/focus).

The `type=rich-inline` variant is implemented as a separate component, `RichTextArea` (molecules/text-area/rich). It is an inline entity-tagging mode - visually identical to `default`, the difference is entirely behavioral: `/` opens a grouped entity picker and each choice is inserted inline as a navigational tag. It is separate rather than a `type` prop because its value (a structured node array), its callbacks (`onSearch`), and its surface (contenteditable) are all disjoint from the plain <textarea>. TextArea therefore still exposes no `type` prop; reach for RichTextArea instead.

Adds a `resize` prop (none/vertical/horizontal/both, default vertical) mapping to the CSS `resize` property - not a Figma axis, but the standard, expected control for a text area. A disabled field locks resize to none.

size.description: Padding, radius, and font size. body-md at sm/md, body-lg at lg. Auto-resize starts at the matching TextField control height.

appearance.description: default = bordered box (all corners rounded). subtle = transparent until hover/focus/invalid, bottom accent only, square bottom corners. inline = chromeless at rest, subtle-style bottom-only border on hover/focus/invalid, keeps padding and top-corner radius — for embedding inside Key Value Pair wrapped in Inline Edit. Figma names this axis `tone`; the inline value maps from Figma's separate `context` axis.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and paints the error border (via box-shadow, no layout shift).

resize.description: Which edges the user can drag. Maps to CSS `resize`. Disabled fields lock to none.

autoResize.description: Grow and shrink with content, starting at the matching control-size height. Overrides rows and manual resizing; remeasures on value and width changes.

maxRows.description: Maximum visible lines with autoResize before vertical scrolling.

disabled.description: Native textarea disabled; greys the frame and locks resize.

rows.description: Native attribute controlling initial height; overridden by autoResize.

iconAfter.description: A trailing icon or interactive control (e.g. an edit pencil IconButton) rendered after the textarea. Not aria-hidden - it may hold a real focusable action.

className.description: Composes with the wrapper div's class list.

...rest.description: Every native textarea attribute (value, defaultValue, placeholder, maxLength, onChange, name, required, readOnly, wrap, ...) forwards to the element. A ref forwards to the <textarea>.

default.purpose: The standard bordered box, rounded on all four corners. Correct for nearly every case.

subtle.purpose: No visible border/background until hover/focus/invalid; a bottom accent line only, square bottom corners. For an inline or low-chrome area that shouldn't compete with surrounding content until used.

inline.purpose: Chromeless at rest with subtle-style bottom-only border on hover/focus/invalid. Keeps the field's normal padding, height, and top-corner radius so it reads as a real input when activated. For embedding inside Key Value Pair wrapped in Inline Edit.

accessibility.label: No built-in label - pair with a native <label htmlFor> or aria-label, the same as Text Field and any native form control.
accessibility.invalid: aria-invalid reflects the invalid prop; the error is also conveyed visually by the border.
accessibility.disabled: native disabled - removed from the tab order and non-editable.
accessibility.focus: the wrapper's own focus border is the focus affordance (via :focus-within, since the focusable textarea is a child of the wrapper).
accessibility.iconAfter: iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden - it may hold a real interactive control (e.g. an IconButton) which must keep its own accessible name and stay keyboard-reachable.

tokens.note: All reused from Text Field - no new tokens. See apiAdaptationNotes for the Figma `background/input/*` -> `elevation/surface/raised/*` naming mapping.

do: Give the textarea an accessible name (a wired <label htmlFor> or aria-label).
Use Text Area for multi-line free text; use Text Field for a single line.
Set `rows` to a sensible initial height for the expected content.
Keep `resize="vertical"` (the default) unless a fixed layout truly needs `none`.
dont: Don't use Text Area for a single-line value - use Text Field.
Don't use it to choose from a fixed set of options - use Select.
Don't use Text Area when the text needs to link to records - use RichTextArea, its inline entity-tagging sibling.
behaviorNotes: The frame styling lives on a wrapper <div>, matching Text Field's pattern. The <textarea> is a transparent, borderless child inside it.
Focus detection uses :focus-within on the wrapper (not :focus on the textarea directly).
Focus/invalid paint the thicker border via inset box-shadow on the wrapper, so the text never shifts.
Hover tint is suppressed once the field is focused.
A disabled field cannot be resized.
iconAfter renders a trailing icon or interactive control at the end of the wrapper row.
appearance='inline' is chromeless at rest with subtle-style bottom-only border on hover/focus/invalid — keeps padding, height, and top-corner radius.
knownLimitations: No built-in label, helper text, or character-count chrome - compose those around it (a Form Field pattern is a natural future step, as noted for Text Field).
futureEnhancements: A shared Form Field wrapper composing label + control + helper/error for both Text Field and Text Area.
